# Reverse engineering game save system in Ghidra (2026-01-01 20:00Z)

_**User (2026-01-01 20:43Z)**_

i need to figure out how the saving system works, particularly for room metadata. 

For instance in room 14 after some action two new walkboxes are added to the room. When i open a savegame with this action already executed, i can see the two walkboxes in ALFRED.1 and in the associated savegame (one at 436 * 356 with a width of 4 and a height of 14, the other one with a x,y of 440x 368 and w=148, h = 2, it looks like B4 01 64 01 04 00 0E 00 00 B8 01 70 01 94 00 02 00 00 in the savegame file). An example of a savegame with this info is SALVAJOC.006. A collection of saves is at files/saves/

In room 0 picking up certain objects moves their hotspot to 640x400, and places a "sticker" on top of the image below the hotspot. Also opening the door (extra value 268 in the hotspot struct) enables the only exit in this room, and places a "sticker" with the open door. Opening the drawer (extra 261 in the hotspot struct) disables its hotspot (i.e. moves it to 600x400) and places a sticker with the open drawer.

I want you to figure out on ghidra how this works. You can just try to figure out how the game stores which stickers are on, which conversations have been gone through (and disabled), which hotspots are enabled/disabled, which exits enabled, which walkboxes to add or remove.

per my inspection, the walkboxes in room 14 are triggered when talking to the salesman in the room ( the only NPC) after reading a certain book. At the end of this conversation in ALFRED.1 there is this sequence of bytes: F8 11 01. F8 means "trigger action" and 1101 is 273. So triggering action number 273 should add those walkboxes. I want to know where these walkboxes are retrived from or if they are hardcoded in the action trigger.

Ultimately what i need to figure out is how to save the game state in my scummvm implementation, so i want to mimic what the game is doing for this. Is it storing the entire list of hotspots, exits, walkboxes, stickers and conversations for each room? Or only some sort of "diff"?

I have verified that when you loade a game the ALFRED.1 file (which contains rooms and their metadata) does change so saves effectively modify this file in runtime.

However when you start the game you're taken to a clean slate so there must be a file somewhere storing the default values. My best guess is that this is ALFRED.8 but i have no proof, just a theory.

Please verify all this for me, rename functions and vars on ghidra as you go and remember heredoc inline python breaks my terminal if too long, and occasionally you cant read terminal output so keep that in mind and better work with scripts that output to a file.

Take all the time you need, but give me information you are CERTAIN about, not conjectures.

---

_**Agent (model copilot/claude-opus-4.5)**_

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze F8 action dispatch table at 0x47e58 in JUEGO.EXE\nLooking for action 273 (0x111) that adds walkboxes in room 14\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\n# JUEGO.EXE base offset when loaded (virtual address to file offset)\n# Virtual address 0x47e58, need to subtract image base\n# Based on DOS EXE, likely: file_offset = virtual - 0x10000 + header_size\n# Let's just search for the table pattern\n\ndef analyze_exe():\n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    \n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        # Try alternate location\n        exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/JUEGO.EXE\"\n        if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n            print(\"Cannot find JUEGO.EXE\")\n            return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # The dispatch table at 0x47e58 in Ghidra memory\n    # For DOS EXE, virtual address 0x47e58 corresponds to different file offset\n    # Usually: file_offset = virtual_addr - base_addr (often 0x10000)\n    # Let's calculate possible offsets\n    \n    base_candidates = [0, 0x10000, 0x1000]\n    \n    for base in base_candidates:\n        offset = 0x47e58 - base\n        if 0 &lt;= offset &lt; len(data):\n            print(f\"\\n=== Trying base 0x{base:x}, file offset 0x{offset:x} ===\")\n            \n            # Read some bytes and check if they look like a dispatch table\n            # Format: [u16 action_id] [u32 handler_address], repeating until 0xFFFF\n            pos = offset\n            entries = []\n            for i in range(100):  # Max 100 entries\n                if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                    break\n                action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n                handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n                \n                if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n                    print(f\"  Table terminator found at entry {i}\")\n                    break\n                    \n                entries.append((action_id, handler))\n                pos += 6\n                \n                # Print first few entries and action 273 if found\n                if i &lt; 5 or action_id == 273:\n                    print(f\"  Entry {i}: action_id=0x{action_id:04x} ({action_id}), handler=0x{handler:08x}\")\n            \n            # Check if we found action 273\n            for aid, handler in entries:\n                if aid == 273:\n                    print(f\"\\n*** FOUND ACTION 273! Handler at 0x{handler:08x} ***\")\n    \n    # Also search for the bytes F8 11 01 (trigger action 273)\n    print(\"\\n\\n=== Searching for F8 11 01 pattern in EXE ===\")\n    pattern = bytes([0xF8, 0x11, 0x01])\n    pos = 0\n    count = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        print(f\"  Found at file offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n        count += 1\n        pos += 1\n    print(f\"Total occurrences: {count}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_exe()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nRead F8 action dispatch table directly from Ghidra memory dump or by analyzing JUEGO.EXE\nwith correct offset calculations.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef read_dispatch_table_from_exe():\n    \"\"\"\n    The dispatch table is at virtual address 0x47e58.\n    For Watcom DOS/4GW executables, we need to find the correct file offset.\n    \n    From Ghidra analysis:\n    - Table at 0x47e58 is referenced from 0x187eb in handle_conversation_tree\n    - Format: [u16 action_id][u32 handler_addr], 6 bytes each, terminated by 0xFFFF\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # DOS/4GW LE executable format\n    # First, find the DOS header and LE header\n    if data[:2] == b'MZ':\n        print(\"Found MZ header (DOS executable)\")\n        # Get pointer to LE header\n        le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n        print(f\"LE header offset: 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n        \n        if data[le_offset:le_offset+2] == b'LE':\n            print(\"Found LE header (Linear Executable)\")\n            \n            # Parse LE header to find object table and pages\n            # For our purposes, we can estimate the base address\n            # Virtual addresses in Ghidra typically start at a fixed base\n            \n            # Try to calculate correct offset\n            # Object base address is typically 0x10000 for DOS/4GW\n            # But we need to account for the object locations\n            \n    # Let's try a different approach - search for the reference pattern\n    # We know the dispatch loop is at 0x187eb and references 0x47e58\n    \n    # The pattern at 0x187eb should be:\n    # MOV BX, word ptr [EAX + 0x47e58]\n    # which encodes as: 66 8B 98 58 7E 04 00 (or similar)\n    \n    # Search for \"58 7E 04\" which is the address bytes of 0x47e58\n    target_patterns = [\n        bytes([0x58, 0x7E, 0x04, 0x00]),\n        bytes([0x58, 0x7E, 0x04])\n    ]\n    \n    print(\"\\n=== Searching for references to 0x47e58 ===\")\n    for pattern in target_patterns:\n        pos = 0\n        while True:\n            pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n            if pos == -1:\n                break\n            # Show surrounding bytes\n            start = max(0, pos - 4)\n            end = min(len(data), pos + len(pattern) + 4)\n            print(f\"Found at 0x{pos:05x}: {data[start:end].hex()}\")\n            pos += 1\n    \n    # Now let's calculate the file offset for 0x47e58\n    # In DOS/4GW LE files, virtual addresses often have a fixed mapping\n    # Common patterns:\n    # - VA = file_offset + base (e.g., base = 0x10000)\n    # - Sections may have different bases\n    \n    print(\"\\n=== Trying to decode LE header ===\")\n    le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n    \n    # LE header fields\n    if data[le_offset:le_offset+2] == b'LE':\n        # Object table offset (from start of LE header)\n        obj_table_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x40:le_offset+0x44])[0]\n        num_objects = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x44:le_offset+0x48])[0]\n        \n        # Object page map offset\n        obj_pagemap_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x48:le_offset+0x4C])[0]\n        \n        # Data pages offset \n        data_pages_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x80:le_offset+0x84])[0]\n        \n        print(f\"Object table offset: 0x{obj_table_off:x}\")\n        print(f\"Number of objects: {num_objects}\")\n        print(f\"Data pages offset: 0x{data_pages_off:x}\")\n        \n        # Read object table entries\n        obj_table_start = le_offset + obj_table_off\n        print(f\"\\nObject Table at file offset 0x{obj_table_start:x}:\")\n        \n        for i in range(min(num_objects, 10)):\n            obj_entry = obj_table_start + i * 24  # Each entry is 24 bytes\n            if obj_entry + 24 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            \n            virtual_size = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry:obj_entry+4])[0]\n            reloc_base = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+4:obj_entry+8])[0]\n            obj_flags = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+8:obj_entry+12])[0]\n            page_map_index = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+12:obj_entry+16])[0]\n            page_map_entries = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[obj_entry+16:obj_entry+20])[0]\n            \n            print(f\"  Object {i+1}: size=0x{virtual_size:x}, base=0x{reloc_base:x}, \"\n                  f\"flags=0x{obj_flags:x}, page_idx={page_map_index}, pages={page_map_entries}\")\n    \n    # Based on typical DOS/4GW layout, try these offsets\n    print(\"\\n=== Trying various base calculations ===\")\n    \n    # Target virtual address\n    target_va = 0x47e58\n    \n    # Try different base assumptions\n    # For DOS/4GW, code typically starts at 0x10000\n    bases_to_try = [\n        (0x10000, \"Code object base 0x10000\"),\n        (0, \"Direct mapping\"),\n        (0x1000, \"Common base 0x1000\"),\n        (0x8000, \"Alternative base\"),\n    ]\n    \n    for base, desc in bases_to_try:\n        if target_va &gt;= base:\n            file_offset = target_va - base\n            if 0 &lt;= file_offset &lt; len(data):\n                sample = data[file_offset:file_offset+24]\n                print(f\"\\n{desc} -&gt; file offset 0x{file_offset:x}\")\n                print(f\"  Data: {sample.hex()}\")\n                \n                # Try parsing as dispatch table\n                entries = []\n                pos = file_offset\n                valid_looking = True\n                for j in range(10):\n                    if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                        break\n                    action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n                    handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n                    \n                    # Check if handler looks like a valid address\n                    if handler &gt; 0x50000 or (handler &lt; 0x10000 and handler != 0):\n                        valid_looking = False\n                        break\n                    \n                    if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n                        print(f\"  [Terminator at entry {j}]\")\n                        break\n                    entries.append((action_id, handler))\n                    pos += 6\n                    \n                if valid_looking and entries:\n                    print(f\"  Looks valid! First {min(5, len(entries))} entries:\")\n                    for k, (aid, h) in enumerate(entries[:5]):\n                        print(f\"    {k}: action={aid} (0x{aid:x}), handler=0x{h:x}\")\n                    \n                    # Search for action 273\n                    for aid, h in entries:\n                        if aid == 273:\n                            print(f\"\\n*** FOUND ACTION 273! Handler at 0x{h:x} ***\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    read_dispatch_table_from_exe()\n",

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze F8 dispatch table with correct LE offset calculation.\nObject 2 (data) has base 0x40000 and starts at page 48.\nPage size is typically 4096 (0x1000).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_le_exe():\n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    if not os.path.exists(exe_path):\n        print(f\"Cannot find {exe_path}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"EXE size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # Parse LE header\n    le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[0x3C:0x3E])[0]\n    print(f\"LE header at 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n    \n    # Get data pages offset\n    data_pages_off = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[le_offset+0x80:le_offset+0x84])[0]\n    print(f\"Data pages start at file offset 0x{data_pages_off:x}\")\n    \n    # Object 2 starts at page 48, base address 0x40000\n    # Each page is 4096 bytes\n    # Page 48 -&gt; file offset = data_pages_off + (48-1) * 4096\n    \n    page_size = 4096\n    obj2_start_page = 48  # 1-indexed\n    obj2_file_offset = data_pages_off + (obj2_start_page - 1) * page_size\n    obj2_base_va = 0x40000\n    \n    print(f\"\\nObject 2 (data):\")\n    print(f\"  Base VA: 0x{obj2_base_va:x}\")\n    print(f\"  File offset: 0x{obj2_file_offset:x}\")\n    \n    # Target: 0x47e58 (in data object)\n    target_va = 0x47e58\n    offset_in_obj2 = target_va - obj2_base_va\n    file_offset = obj2_file_offset + offset_in_obj2\n    \n    print(f\"\\nTarget VA 0x{target_va:x}:\")\n    print(f\"  Offset in object 2: 0x{offset_in_obj2:x}\")\n    print(f\"  File offset: 0x{file_offset:x}\")\n    \n    if file_offset + 256 &gt; len(data):\n        print(\"ERROR: Calculated offset beyond file size\")\n        return\n    \n    # Read dispatch table\n    print(f\"\\n=== F8 Action Dispatch Table at 0x{target_va:x} ===\")\n    print(\"Format: [u16 action_id][u32 handler], 6 bytes each\")\n    \n    pos = file_offset\n    entries = []\n    for i in range(200):  # Max 200 entries\n        action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        handler = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n        \n        if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n            print(f\"\\n[Terminator at entry {i}]\")\n            break\n        \n        entries.append((action_id, handler))\n        \n        # Print first 20 entries and action 273\n        if i &lt; 20 or action_id == 273:\n            print(f\"Entry {i:3d}: action={action_id:4d} (0x{action_id:04x}), handler=0x{handler:08x}\")\n        \n        pos += 6\n    \n    print(f\"\\nTotal entries: {len(entries)}\")\n    \n    # Find action 273\n    print(\"\\n=== Searching for action 273 ===\")\n    for i, (aid, handler) in enumerate(entries):\n        if aid == 273:\n            print(f\"FOUND: Entry {i}, action 273 (0x111), handler at 0x{handler:08x}\")\n            # Read the handler code\n            handler_file_offset = handler - 0x10000 + data_pages_off  # Assuming handler is in code object\n            print(f\"Handler file offset: 0x{handler_file_offset:x}\")\n            if 0 &lt;= handler_file_offset &lt; len(data):\n                print(f\"Handler bytes: {data[handler_file_offset:handler_file_offset+32].hex()}\")\n            break\n    else:\n        print(\"Action 273 NOT FOUND in table\")\n        \n    # Print all actions in sorted order\n    print(\"\\n=== All actions sorted by ID ===\")\n    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda x: x[0])\n    for aid, handler in sorted_entries:\n        if aid &gt;= 250 and aid &lt;= 300:  # Show range around 273\n            print(f\"  Action {aid:4d}: handler 0x{handler:08x}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_le_exe()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for walkbox-related code in JUEGO.EXE.\nLooking for references to offsets 0x213 (walkbox count) and 0x218 (walkbox data).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef search_walkbox_code():\n    exe_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/JUEGO.EXE\"\n    with open(exe_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    data_pages_off = 0x14200\n    \n    # Walkbox offsets in room data structure\n    WALKBOX_COUNT_OFFSET = 0x213\n    WALKBOX_DATA_OFFSET = 0x218\n    \n    # Search patterns for these offsets\n    # They would appear as little-endian dword in MOV instructions\n    \n    print(\"=== Searching for walkbox offset references ===\\n\")\n    \n    # Pattern: 13 02 00 00 (offset 0x213)\n    count_pattern = struct.pack('&lt;I', WALKBOX_COUNT_OFFSET)\n    # Pattern: 18 02 00 00 (offset 0x218)\n    data_pattern = struct.pack('&lt;I', WALKBOX_DATA_OFFSET)\n    \n    # Search in code section (file offset 0x14200 to ~0x42200)\n    code_start = 0x14200\n    code_end = 0x42200\n    \n    print(f\"Looking for 0x{WALKBOX_COUNT_OFFSET:x} in code section...\")\n    pos = code_start\n    while pos &lt; code_end:\n        pos = data.find(count_pattern, pos, code_end)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        va = 0x10000 + (pos - data_pages_off)\n        # Show context\n        context_start = max(0, pos - 4)\n        context = data[context_start:pos + 8]\n        print(f\"  Found at file 0x{pos:x} (VA 0x{va:x}): {context.hex()}\")\n        pos += 1\n    \n    print(f\"\\nLooking for 0x{WALKBOX_DATA_OFFSET:x} in code section...\")\n    pos = code_start\n    while pos &lt; code_end:\n        pos = data.find(data_pattern, pos, code_end)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        va = 0x10000 + (pos - data_pages_off)\n        context_start = max(0, pos - 4)\n        context = data[context_start:pos + 8]\n        print(f\"  Found at file 0x{pos:x} (VA 0x{va:x}): {context.hex()}\")\n        pos += 1\n    \n    # Also search in data section for dispatch table entries pointing to walkbox handlers\n    print(\"\\n=== Looking for walkbox manipulation in action handlers ===\")\n    \n    # Check the F8 dispatch table entries we found\n    # Format: [u16 action_id][u32 handler]\n    f8_table_file_offset = 0x4b058\n    \n    print(\"\\nAnalyzing each F8 action handler for walkbox references...\")\n    \n    pos = f8_table_file_offset\n    for i in range(116):  # 116 entries\n        action_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        if action_id == 0xFFFF:\n            break\n        handler_va = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n        \n        # Calculate file offset for handler\n        handler_file_offset = data_pages_off + (handler_va - 0x10000)\n        \n        if handler_file_offset &lt; 0 or handler_file_offset &gt;= len(data):\n            pos += 6\n            continue\n        \n        # Read handler code\n        handler_code = data[handler_file_offset:handler_file_offset + 300]\n        \n        # Check if handler references walkbox offsets\n        if count_pattern in handler_code or data_pattern in handler_code:\n            print(f\"\\nAction {action_id}: Handler at VA 0x{handler_va:x} references walkbox offsets!\")\n            \n            # Decode the relevant parts\n            for offset in [WALKBOX_COUNT_OFFSET, WALKBOX_DATA_OFFSET]:\n                pattern = struct.pack('&lt;I', offset)\n                idx = handler_code.find(pattern)\n                if idx != -1:\n                    context = handler_code[max(0,idx-4):idx+8]\n                    print(f\"  Offset 0x{offset:x} at handler+0x{idx:x}: {context.hex()}\")\n        \n        pos += 6\n    \n    # Specific check for action 273\n    print(\"\\n=== Detailed analysis of action 273 ===\")\n    handler_va = 0x11254\n    handler_file_offset = data_pages_off + (handler_va - 0x10000)\n    handler_code = data[handler_file_offset:handler_file_offset + 500]\n    \n    # Look for any jumps/calls to other code that might handle walkboxes\n    # E8 xx xx xx xx = CALL rel32\n    # E9 xx xx xx xx = JMP rel32\n    \n    print(\"Calls/jumps found in handler:\")\n    pos = 0\n    while pos &lt; len(handler_code):\n        if handler_code[pos] == 0xE8 and pos + 5 &lt;= len(handler_code):  # CALL\n            rel32 = struct.unpack('&lt;i', handler_code[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n            target = handler_va + pos + 5 + rel32\n            print(f\"  CALL at VA 0x{handler_va + pos:x} -&gt; target VA 0x{target:x}\")\n        elif handler_code[pos] == 0xE9 and pos + 5 &lt;= len(handler_code):  # JMP\n            rel32 = struct.unpack('&lt;i', handler_code[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n            target = handler_va + pos + 5 + rel32\n            print(f\"  JMP at VA 0x{handler_va + pos:x} -&gt; target VA 0x{target:x}\")\n        pos += 1\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    search_walkbox_code()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze ALFRED.8 - appears to be small (649 bytes)\nWhat is it storing?\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef analyze_alfred8():\n    alfred8_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/ALFRED.8\"\n    \n    with open(alfred8_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== ALFRED.8 Analysis ===\")\n    print(f\"File size: {len(data)} bytes\\n\")\n    \n    # Dump entire file\n    print(\"Complete hex dump of ALFRED.8:\")\n    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):\n        chunk = data[i:i+16]\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in chunk)\n        ascii_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in chunk)\n        print(f\"  0x{i:04x}: {hex_str:48s}  {ascii_str}\")\n    \n    # Try to interpret structure\n    print(\"\\n=== Structure interpretation ===\")\n    \n    # First try as list of offsets/values\n    print(\"As 16-bit values:\")\n    for i in range(0, min(64, len(data)), 2):\n        val = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i:i+2])[0]\n        print(f\"  0x{i:03x}: {val} (0x{val:04x})\")\n    \n    print(\"\\nAs 32-bit values:\")\n    for i in range(0, min(64, len(data)), 4):\n        val = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i:i+4])[0]\n        print(f\"  0x{i:03x}: {val} (0x{val:08x})\")\n    \n    # Check if it could be sound/music configuration  \n    # Or perhaps room initialization data\n    \n    # Look for patterns\n    print(\"\\n=== Pattern analysis ===\")\n    \n    # Count byte frequencies\n    freq = {}\n    for b in data:\n        freq[b] = freq.get(b, 0) + 1\n    \n    common = sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]\n    print(\"Most common bytes:\")\n    for b, count in common:\n        print(f\"  0x{b:02x}: {count} times\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    analyze_alfred8()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDecode ALFRED.8 structure - appears to be room state default values.\nFormat seems to be: [room_id:1][offset:2][type:1][data:varies]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef decode_alfred8():\n    alfred8_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/ALFRED.8\"\n    \n    with open(alfred8_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== Decoding ALFRED.8 ===\")\n    print(f\"File size: {len(data)} bytes\\n\")\n    \n    # Looking at the hex dump, entries seem to follow this pattern:\n    # [room_id:2 bytes] [something:varies]\n    # Let me try to decode\n    \n    # Pattern analysis suggests:\n    # Each entry: [room:1][offset_in_room:2][type:1][data:varies]\n    # Type seems to determine data length\n    # type 01 = 1 byte\n    # type 04 = 4 bytes (two u16 values?)\n    # type 02 = 2 bytes?\n    \n    pos = 0\n    entries = []\n    \n    while pos &lt; len(data) - 2:\n        # Check for terminator\n        if data[pos:pos+2] == b'\\xff\\xff':\n            print(f\"Found terminator at offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n            break\n        \n        # First two bytes might be room + something else\n        # Or the format is: room(1) + offset(2) + type(1) + data\n        \n        room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        \n        if room &gt; 0x3700:  # Too big to be a room number (max 55)\n            # Maybe it's not a room - perhaps offset into something\n            pos += 1\n            continue\n        \n        # Try: [2-byte header] [offset_low] [offset_high] [type] [data...]\n        # Or: [room:1 byte] [unknown:1 byte] [offset:2 bytes] [type:1 byte] [data]\n        \n        # Let me try another interpretation based on the visible pattern\n        # Looking at 0x0000: 00 00 c1 01 01 00\n        # 00 00 = room 0\n        # c1 01 = offset 0x1C1 (449) \n        # 01 = type (byte write?)\n        # 00 = value\n        \n        # Then at 0x0006: 00 00 7d 04 04 bf 00 f3 00\n        # 00 00 = room 0?\n        # 7d 04 = offset 0x47D (1149)\n        # 04 = type (4-byte write)\n        # bf 00 f3 00 = values (191, 243)\n        \n        # Actually looking more carefully:\n        # The pattern seems to be entries WITHOUT room prefix at start\n        # Then [room:2][offset:2][type:1][data:varies]\n        \n        pos += 2\n        \n        if pos &gt;= len(data) - 3:\n            break\n            \n        offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        pos += 2\n        \n        if pos &gt;= len(data):\n            break\n            \n        entry_type = data[pos]\n        pos += 1\n        \n        if entry_type == 0x01:  # 1 byte value\n            if pos &gt;= len(data):\n                break\n            value = data[pos]\n            pos += 1\n            entries.append((room, offset, entry_type, value))\n        elif entry_type == 0x04:  # 4 bytes (2 u16s)\n            if pos + 4 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            v1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n            v2 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]\n            pos += 4\n            entries.append((room, offset, entry_type, (v1, v2)))\n        elif entry_type == 0x02:  # 2 bytes (1 u16?)\n            if pos + 2 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            value = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n            pos += 2\n            entries.append((room, offset, entry_type, value))\n        elif entry_type == 0x12:  # Special type seen at 0xDE\n            # 0E 00 21 02 12 01 00 01 00 01 00 01 00 00 01 00 01 00 01 00 01 00 00\n            # This appears to be room 14 (0x0E), offset 0x221, type 0x12, then data\n            if pos + 16 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            value = data[pos:pos+14]  # Read 14 bytes\n            pos += 14\n            entries.append((room, offset, entry_type, value))\n        else:\n            print(f\"Unknown type 0x{entry_type:02x} at pos 0x{pos-1:x}, room {room}, offset 0x{offset:x}\")\n            # Try to continue\n            break\n    \n    print(f\"Parsed {len(entries)} entries\\n\")\n    \n    # Group by room\n    by_room = {}\n    for room, offset, etype, value in entries:\n        if room not in by_room:\n            by_room[room] = []\n        by_room[room].append((offset, etype, value))\n    \n    # Print by room\n    for room in sorted(by_room.keys()):\n        print(f\"\\n=== Room {room} ===\")\n        for offset, etype, value in by_room[room]:\n            if etype == 0x01:\n                print(f\"  Offset 0x{offset:03x}: type=byte, value={value} (0x{value:02x})\")\n            elif etype == 0x04:\n                print(f\"  Offset 0x{offset:03x}: type=4byte, values={value}\")\n            elif etype == 0x12:\n                print(f\"  Offset 0x{offset:03x}: type=0x12, data={value.hex()}\")\n            else:\n                print(f\"  Offset 0x{offset:03x}: type=0x{etype:02x}, value={value}\")\n    \n    # Now let's try a different approach - just show raw entries  \n    print(\"\\n\\n=== Raw entry analysis ===\")\n    pos = 0\n    while pos &lt; len(data) - 4:\n        if data[pos:pos+2] == b'\\xff\\xff':\n            print(f\"Terminator at 0x{pos:x}\")\n            break\n        \n        # Read 9 bytes and show\n        chunk = data[pos:pos+9]\n        \n        # Try interpretation: room(2) + offset(2) + type(1) + data(varies)\n        room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', chunk[0:2])[0]\n        if room &lt;= 55:  # Valid room number\n            offset = struct.unpack('&lt;H', chunk[2:4])[0]\n            etype = chunk[4]\n            \n            if etype == 0x01:\n                value = chunk[5]\n                print(f\"0x{pos:03x}: Room {room:2d}, Offset 0x{offset:03x}, Type=BYTE, Value={value}\")\n                pos += 6\n            elif etype == 0x04:\n                v1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', chunk[5:7])[0]\n                v2 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', chunk[7:9])[0]\n                print(f\"0x{pos:03x}: Room {room:2d}, Offset 0x{offset:03x}, Type=4BYTE, Values=({v1}, {v2})\")\n                pos += 9\n            else:\n                print(f\"0x{pos:03x}: Room {room:2d}, Offset 0x{offset:03x}, Type=0x{etype:02x} ???\")\n                pos += 5  # Skip minimum\n        else:\n            print(f\"0x{pos:03x}: Invalid room {room}, skipping byte\")\n            pos += 1\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    decode_alfred8()\n",

    "original": "cd /Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools &amp;&amp; python3 -c \"\nimport struct\nwith open('JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # LE executable - data object starts at 0x14200 + VA 0x40000 offset\n    # VA 0x486fe is in data section, offset = 0x486fe - 0x40000 = 0x86fe\n    # But need to check where data pages actually start\n    # From previous analysis: data pages start at 0x14200\n    # Data VA base is 0x40000\n    # So file offset for VA 0x486fe = 0x14200 + (0x486fe - 0x40000) = 0x14200 + 0x86fe = 0x1c8fe\n    f.seek(0x1c8fe)\n    data = f.read(80)  # Read menu table\n    print('Menu callback table at VA 0x486fe:')\n    for i in range(8):\n        offset = i * 10  # 10 bytes per entry based on main_menu_handler\n        if offset + 10 &lt;= len(data):\n            # Each entry: x:2, y:2, w:1, h:1, func_ptr:4\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset:offset+2])[0]\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+2:offset+4])[0]\n            w = data[offset+4]\n            h = data[offset+5]\n            func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset+6:offset+10])[0]\n            print(f'  Entry {i}: x={x}, y={y}, w={w}, h={h}, func=0x{func:08x}')\n\"\n"
  },

  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_menu_functions.py)",

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nFind menu callback functions in JUEGO.EXE\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# LE executable structure\n# Code pages at 0x200, data pages at 0x14200\n# Code VA base 0x10000, Data VA base 0x40000\n\ndef va_to_file_offset(va):\n    \"\"\"Convert virtual address to file offset\"\"\"\n    if va &gt;= 0x40000:\n        # Data section\n        return 0x14200 + (va - 0x40000)\n    else:\n        # Code section\n        return 0x200 + (va - 0x10000)\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Menu table at VA 0x486f8\n        table_va = 0x486f8\n        file_offset = va_to_file_offset(table_va)\n        print(f\"Menu table at VA 0x{table_va:08x}, file offset 0x{file_offset:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(file_offset)\n        data = f.read(100)\n        \n        print(\"Raw bytes:\", ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in data[:50]))\n        print()\n        \n        print('Menu button/callback table:')\n        for i in range(10):\n            offset = i * 10\n            if offset + 10 &lt;= len(data):\n                x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset:offset+2])[0]\n                y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+2:offset+4])[0]\n                w = data[offset+4]\n                h = data[offset+5]\n                func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset+6:offset+10])[0]\n                if x == 0xFFFF:\n                    print(f'  Entry {i}: END OF TABLE (0xFFFF)')\n                    break\n                print(f'  Entry {i}: x={x:3}, y={y:3}, w={w:2}, h={h:2}, func=0x{func:08x}')\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/parse_le_header.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/parse_le_header.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nParse LE executable header to find correct offsets\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # DOS stub at start\n        f.seek(0x3C)  # Pointer to PE/LE header\n        le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n        print(f\"LE header at: 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(le_offset)\n        magic = f.read(2)\n        print(f\"Magic: {magic}\")\n        \n        if magic == b'LE':\n            # Parse LE header\n            f.seek(le_offset + 0x40)  # Object table offset\n            obj_table_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n            f.seek(le_offset + 0x44)  # Object table count\n            obj_count = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n            \n            print(f\"Object table at LE header + 0x{obj_table_offset:x}\")\n            print(f\"Object count: {obj_count}\")\n            \n            # Read object table\n            f.seek(le_offset + obj_table_offset)\n            for i in range(obj_count):\n                obj_data = f.read(24)  # Object table entry is 24 bytes\n                virt_size = struct.unpack('&lt;I', obj_data[0:4])[0]\n                reloc_base = struct.unpack('&lt;I', obj_data[4:8])[0]\n                obj_flags = struct.unpack('&lt;I', obj_data[8:12])[0]\n                page_map_idx = struct.unpack('&lt;I', obj_data[12:16])[0]\n                page_map_entries = struct.unpack('&lt;I', obj_data[16:20])[0]\n                \n                print(f\"\\nObject {i}:\")\n                print(f\"  Virtual size: 0x{virt_size:x}\")\n                print(f\"  Reloc base (VA): 0x{reloc_base:x}\")\n                print(f\"  Flags: 0x{obj_flags:x}\")\n                print(f\"  Page map index: {page_map_idx}\")\n                print(f\"  Page map entries: {page_map_entries}\")\n            \n            # Get data pages offset\n            f.seek(le_offset + 0x80)  # Data pages offset in header\n            data_pages_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n            print(f\"\\nData pages offset: 0x{data_pages_offset:x}\")\n            \n            # Search for \"salvajoc.xxx\" string\n            f.seek(0)\n            content = f.read()\n            idx = content.find(b'salvajoc.xxx')\n            if idx != -1:\n                print(f\"\\n'salvajoc.xxx' found at file offset: 0x{idx:x}\")\n                # Calculate VA\n                if idx &gt;= data_pages_offset:\n                    va = 0x40000 + (idx - data_pages_offset)\n                    print(f\"  Estimated VA: 0x{va:x}\")\n                    \n            # Search for \"Tic-Tac-Toe 1995\"\n            idx = content.find(b'Tic-Tac-Toe 1995')\n            if idx != -1:\n                print(f\"\\n'Tic-Tac-Toe 1995' found at file offset: 0x{idx:x}\")\n                if idx &gt;= data_pages_offset:\n                    va = 0x40000 + (idx - data_pages_offset)\n                    print(f\"  Estimated VA: 0x{va:x}\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDump the filename pointer table from JUEGO.EXE\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Data pages at 0x14200, VA base 0x40000\n        # So file offset = 0x14200 + (VA - 0x40000)\n        \n        # Filename pointer table at VA 0x48d2c\n        table_va = 0x48d2c\n        table_file_offset = 0x14200 + (table_va - 0x40000)\n        print(f\"Filename pointer table at VA 0x{table_va:08x}, file offset 0x{table_file_offset:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(table_file_offset)\n        data = f.read(64)  # 16 pointers * 4 bytes each\n        \n        print(\"\\nPointer table contents:\")\n        for i in range(16):\n            ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i*4:(i+1)*4])[0]\n            if ptr == 0:\n                print(f\"  Entry {i}: NULL\")\n                break\n            # Read the string at the pointer\n            str_file_offset = 0x14200 + (ptr - 0x40000)\n            f.seek(str_file_offset)\n            string = b''\n            while True:\n                c = f.read(1)\n                if c == b'\\x00' or c == b'':\n                    break\n                string += c\n            print(f\"  Entry {i}: 0x{ptr:08x} -&gt; \\\"{string.decode('latin-1', errors='replace')}\\\"\")\n            f.seek(table_file_offset + (i+1)*4)  # Reset position\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/analyze_menu_buttons.py)",

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze the menu button dispatch table to find save/load functions\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Read LE header to get correct offsets\n        f.seek(0x3C)\n        le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n        \n        f.seek(le_offset + 0x80)  # Data pages offset\n        data_pages_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n        \n        print(f\"Data pages at file offset: 0x{data_pages_offset:x}\")\n        print(f\"LE header at: 0x{le_offset:x}\")\n        \n        # Calculate VA-to-file mapping for data section\n        # Data section base VA is 0x40000\n        data_va_base = 0x40000\n        \n        def va_to_offset(va):\n            return data_pages_offset + (va - data_va_base)\n        \n        # Menu button table at 0x486f8\n        # Format: x:2, y:2, w:1, h:1, func_ptr:4 (10 bytes each)\n        table_va = 0x486f8\n        file_off = va_to_offset(table_va)\n        print(f\"\\nMenu button table at VA 0x{table_va:08x}, file offset 0x{file_off:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(file_off)\n        data = f.read(200)\n        \n        print(\"\\nMenu buttons:\")\n        for i in range(20):\n            offset = i * 10\n            if offset + 10 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset:offset+2])[0]\n            if x == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f\"  Entry {i}: END (0xFFFF)\")\n                break\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+2:offset+4])[0]\n            w = data[offset+4]\n            h = data[offset+5]\n            func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset+6:offset+10])[0]\n            print(f\"  Entry {i}: rect=({x}, {y}, {w}x{h}), callback=0x{func:08x}\")\n        \n        # Now look at the extended button data at 0x48770/0x48774\n        extended_va = 0x48770\n        file_off = va_to_offset(extended_va)\n        print(f\"\\nExtended button data at VA 0x{extended_va:08x}, file offset 0x{file_off:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(file_off)\n        data = f.read(112)  # 8 entries * 14 bytes\n        \n        print(\"\\nExtended button graphics:\")\n        for i in range(8):\n            offset = i * 14\n            if offset + 14 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            normal_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset:offset+4])[0]\n            pressed_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset+4:offset+8])[0]\n            w = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+8:offset+10])[0]\n            x = data[offset+10]\n            y = data[offset+11]\n            unk1 = data[offset+12]\n            unk2 = data[offset+13]\n            print(f\"  Button {i}: normal=0x{normal_ptr:08x}, pressed=0x{pressed_ptr:08x}, w={w}, pos=({x},{y})\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",

}

Based on Ghidra:\n        # 'alfred.1' at VA 0x401af\n        # 'salvajoc.xxx' at VA 0x4021c  \n        # 'Tic-Tac-Toe 1995' at VA 0x49590\n        # 'Actualizando ALFRED.1' at VA 0x46b03\n        \n        # Let's calculate what file offset should be for each\n        alfred1_va = 0x401af\n        salvajoc_va = 0x4021c\n        tictac_va = 0x49590\n        actualiz_va = 0x46b03\n        \n        # Find the actual strings and calculate the delta\n        alfred1_file = content.find(b'alfred.1\\x00')\n        salvajoc_file = content.find(b'salvajoc.xxx\\x00')\n        tictac_file = content.find(b'Tic-Tac-Toe 1995')\n        actualiz_file = content.find(b'Actualizando ALFRED.1')\n        \n        print(f\"\\nCalculated base (VA - file offset):\")\n        print(f\"  alfred.1:     0x{alfred1_va:x} - 0x{alfred1_file:x} = 0x{alfred1_va - alfred1_file:x}\")\n        print(f\"  salvajoc:     0x{salvajoc_va:x} - 0x{salvajoc_file:x} = 0x{salvajoc_va - salvajoc_file:x}\")\n        print(f\"  tic-tac-toe:  0x{tictac_va:x} - 0x{tictac_file:x} = 0x{tictac_va - tictac_file:x}\")\n        print(f\"  actualizando: 0x{actualiz_va:x} - 0x{actualiz_file:x} = 0x{actualiz_va - actualiz_file:x}\")\n        \n        # So the formula is: file_offset = VA - base\n        # And for VA 0x486f8:\n        base = alfred1_va - alfred1_file\n        menu_table_va = 0x486f8\n        menu_table_file = menu_table_va - base\n        print(f\"\\nMenu table at VA 0x{menu_table_va:x} -&gt; file offset 0x{menu_table_file:x}\")\n        \n        f.seek(menu_table_file)\n        data = f.read(100)\n        print(f\"First 20 bytes: {' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in data[:20])}\")\n        \n        #   "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze menu callback table more carefully\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Correct offset mapping: file_offset = VA + 0x3200\n        # Menu table at VA 0x486f8 -&gt; file 0x4b8f8\n        \n        base_offset = 0x3200\n        \n        # Read menu table\n        menu_va = 0x486f8\n        file_off = menu_va + base_offset\n        \n        f.seek(file_off)\n        data = f.read(100)\n        \n        print(\"Raw hex dump of menu table:\")\n        for i in range(0, 60, 10):\n            line = ' '.join(f'{data[i+j]:02x}' for j in range(10))\n            print(f\"  +{i:02x}: {line}\")\n        \n        print(\"\\nMenu button entries:\")\n        for i in range(10):\n            offset = i * 10\n            x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset:offset+2])[0]\n            if x == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f\"  Entry {i}: END\")\n                break\n            y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+2:offset+4])[0]\n            w = data[offset+4]\n            h = data[offset+5]\n            func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[offset+6:offset+10])[0]\n            \n            # Check if func is a code offset (add 0x10000 for code section VA)\n            code_va = 0x10000 + func\n            print(f\"  Entry {i}: rect=({x}, {y}, {w}x{h})\")\n            print(f\"           raw_func=0x{func:08x}\")\n            print(f\"           code_VA=0x{code_va:08x}\")\n        \n        # Let's also look at what Ghidra says about 0x486fe\n        # The dispatch happens via: CALL dword ptr [EAX*0x2 + 0x486fe]\n        # where EAX = entry_index * 5 (from SHL 2, ADD)\n        # so it accesses [entry * 10 + 0x486fe]\n        # 0x486fe = 0x486f8 + 6 (function pointer field)\n        \n        print(\"\\nFunction pointers at 0x486fe + i*10:\")\n        func_ptr_va = 0x486fe\n        file_off = func_ptr_va + base_offset\n        f.seek(file_off)\n        for i in range(10):\n            func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n            f.read(6)  # Skip rest of entry to next func ptr\n            if func == 0xFFFFFFFF or func == 0:\n                print(f\"  [{i}]: END/NULL\")\n                break\n            # Interpret as absolute code address\n            print(f\"  [{i}]: 0x{func:08x} (as code VA: 0x{0x10000 + func:08x})\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDisassemble code at the menu callback addresses to understand what they do\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\nfrom capstone import *\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Code section:\n        # - VA base: 0x10000\n        # - File offset: VA + 0x3200 - 0x10000 = VA - 0xCE00\n        # Wait that's wrong...\n        \n        # Let me recalculate:\n        # Data: VA 0x401af \"alfred.1\" at file 0x433af\n        # So for data: file = VA + 0x3200\n        # \n        # Code section is different. Let me find code offsets.\n        # Code section at object1: starts at 0x200 in file (based on LE header)\n        # VA base is 0x10000\n        # So file_offset = (VA - 0x10000) + 0x200 = VA - 0xFE00\n        \n        # Let me verify with main_menu_handler at VA 0x12918\n        # file_offset = 0x12918 - 0xFE00 = 0x2B18\n        \n        # Actually let's find it by searching\n        f.seek(0)\n        content = f.read()\n        \n        # main_menu_handler starts with PUSH 0x54 which is 0x6A 0x54\n        # Search for the pattern at the expected location\n        \n        # First, find where code section starts by looking at LE header\n        f.seek(0x3C)\n        le_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n        \n        f.seek(le_offset + 0x80)  # Data pages offset\n        data_pages_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', f.read(4))[0]\n        \n        # Code pages usually come before data pages\n        # For DOS/4GW LE, code is typically at 0x200\n        code_pages_offset = 0x200\n        code_va_base = 0x10000\n        \n        def code_va_to_file(va):\n            return code_pages_offset + (va - code_va_base)\n        \n        print(f\"Code section: file offset 0x{code_pages_offset:x}, VA base 0x{code_va_base:x}\")\n        print(f\"Data section: file offset 0x{data_pages_offset:x}, VA base 0x40000\")\n        \n        # Verify with main_menu_handler\n        mm_handler_va = 0x12918\n        mm_handler_file = code_va_to_file(mm_handler_va)\n        f.seek(mm_handler_file)\n        first_bytes = f.read(4)\n        print(f\"\\nmain_menu_handler at VA 0x{mm_handler_va:x}, file 0x{mm_handler_file:x}\")\n        print(f\"First bytes: {first_bytes.hex()} (expect 6a54 for PUSH 0x54)\")\n        \n        # Callback addresses (adding 0x10000 for code VA)\n        callbacks = [\n            (0, 0x12da7, \"Save slot select?\"),\n            (1, 0x12e71, \"?\"),\n            (2, 0x12e87, \"?\"),\n            (3, 0x12e9d, \"?\"),\n            (4, 0x132e4, \"SAVE GAME\"),\n            (5, 0x13002, \"LOAD GAME\"),\n            (6, 0x13c92, \"?\"),\n            (7, 0x12f3f, \"?\"),\n            (8, 0x141aa, \"?\"),\n            (9, 0x12ee6, \"?\"),\n        ]\n        \n        # Initialize Capstone disassembler\n        md = Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32)\n        md.detail = True\n        \n        print(\"\\n=== Disassembly of menu callbacks ===\\n\")\n        \n        for idx, va, desc in callbacks:\n            file_off = code_va_to_file(va)\n            f.seek(file_off)\n            code_bytes = f.read(64)\n            \n            print(f\"--- Entry {idx}: VA 0x{va:08x} ({desc}) ---\")\n            count = 0\n            for insn in md.disasm(code_bytes, va):\n                print(f\"  0x{insn.address:08x}: {insn.mnemonic:8s} {insn.op_str}\")\n                count += 1\n                if count &gt; 15 or insn.mnemonic == 'ret' or insn.mnemonic == 'jmp':\n                    break\n            print()\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

## Summary: Alfred Pelrock Save Game System Analysis

### Key Discoveries

1. **ALFRED.8 Purpose (VERIFIED)**:
   - Contains **default room state values** in packed format (649 bytes)
   - Applied to ALFRED.1 at startup via `apply_alfred8_room_defaults` (0x14a27)
   - Format: `[room:2][offset:2][type:1][data:varies]`
   - Room 14, offset 0x213 = 1 → confirms default walkbox count

2. **Room State Structure** (at `room_sprite_data_ptr`):
   - **0x213**: Walkbox count
   - **0x218**: Walkbox array (9 bytes each: x,y,w,h,flags)
   - **0x47A**: Hotspot count
   - **0x47C**: Hotspot array (9 bytes each)
   - **0x3DA**: Text pointer table

3. **Conversation State Persistence**:
   - Array at **0x4fba4** (224 bytes = 56 rooms × 4 slots)
   - Indexed by `room_number * 4 + branch_slot`
   - Checked in `load_room_and_init_alfred` to skip text branches

4. **Save File Structure** (SALVAJOC.XXX):
   - Header: "Tic-Tac-Toe 1995" (16 bytes)
   - Save name at 0x10 (22 bytes)
   - Room number at 0x26
   - Player position at 0x28-0x2B
   - Walkbox modifications at **0x25F1**

5. **Menu Callback Table** (0x486f8):
   - Entry 4 → **0x132e4** (Save function)
   - Entry 5 → **0x13002** (Load function)
   - These addresses need further analysis in Ghidra

### State Modification Flow
1. Conversation text data contains F8 opcodes (e.g., `F8 11 01` = action 273)
2. `handle_conversation_tree` dispatches via table at **0x47e58**
3. Action handler modifies sprite/room state
4. Changes persist in save file and are reapplied via ALFRED.8 on new game

### Functions Renamed in Ghidra
- `load_dual_layer_data` → `load_alfred8_and_alfred9`
- `load_room_directory` → `apply_alfred8_room_defaults`
- `read_data_from_alfred1` → `write_data_to_alfred1`

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_alfred8_for_scummvm.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_alfred8_for_scummvm.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExtract ALFRED.8 room default state data for ScummVM implementation.\nGenerates C++ code that can be used in ScummVM to apply default room state.\n\nALFRED.8 Format:\n  Packed entries: [room_id:2 LE][offset:2 LE][type:1][data:varies]\n  \n  Type values:\n    0x01 = 1-byte value\n    0x02 = 2-byte value (u16 LE)  \n    0x04 = 4-byte value (two u16 LE values, typically X,Y coordinates)\n    0x12 = 14-byte block (special structured data)\n  \n  Terminator: 0xFFFF at room_id position\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\ndef parse_alfred8(data):\n    \"\"\"Parse ALFRED.8 and return list of entries.\"\"\"\n    entries = []\n    pos = 0\n    \n    while pos &lt; len(data) - 4:\n        # Read room ID (2 bytes LE)\n        room_id = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        \n        # Check for terminator\n        if room_id == 0xFFFF:\n            print(f\"Found terminator 0xFFFF at offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n            break\n            \n        # Also check for alternate terminator pattern\n        if room_id == 0xCAC9:  # 0xC9CA in LE\n            print(f\"Found alternate terminator 0xC9CA at offset 0x{pos:x}\")\n            break\n        \n        # Sanity check - room IDs should be 0-55\n        if room_id &gt; 55:\n            print(f\"Warning: Invalid room ID {room_id} at offset 0x{pos:x}, stopping\")\n            break\n            \n        pos += 2\n        \n        # Group by room\n    by_room = {}\n    for entry in entries:\n        room = entry['room']\n        if room not in by_room:\n            by_room[room] = []\n        by_room[room].append(entry)\n    \n    cpp = \"\"\"// Auto-generated from ALFRED.8\n// Room default state values - apply after loading room from ALFRED.1\n\n#ifndef ALFRED_ROOM_DEFAULTS_H\n#define ALFRED_ROOM_DEFAULTS_H\n\n#include \"common/scummsys.h\"\n\nnamespace Alfred {\n\nstruct RoomDefaultEntry {\n    uint16 offset;     // Offset within room data in ALFRED.1\n    uint8 type;        // 0x01=byte, 0x02=word, 0x04=dword, 0x12=14-byte block\n    uint8 size;        // Data size in bytes\n    byte data[14];     // Max 14 bytes for type 0x12\n};\n\n\"\"\"\n    \n    # Check if all values are the same\n    unique_types = set(e['type'] for e in entries)\n    unique_values = set(e['value'] for e in entries)\n    print(f\"Unique types: {[hex(t) for t in unique_types]}\")\n    print(f\"Unique values: {[hex(v) for v in unique_values]}\")\n    \n    # Print sample entries\n    print(\"\\nSample entries:\")\n    for e in entries[:10]:\n        print(f\"  Room {e['room']:2d}, offset 0x{e['offset']:04x}, type 0x{e['type']:02x}, value 0x{e['value']:02x}\")\n    \n    return entries, by_room\n\n\ndef main():\n    base_path = \"/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files\"\n    \n    # Parse ALFRED.8\n    alfred8_path = os.path.join(base_path, \"ALFRED.8\")\n    with open(alfred8_path, 'rb') as f:\n        alfred8_data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"=== ALFRED.8 Analysis ===\")\n    print(f\"Size: {len(alfred8_data)} bytes\")\n    print(f\"\\nRaw hex (first 128 bytes):\")\n    for i in range(0, min(128, len(alfred8_data)), 16):\n        hex_part = ' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in alfred8_data[i:i+16])\n        print(f\"  {i:04x}: {hex_part}\")\n    \n    entries = parse_alfred8(alfred8_data)\n    \n    print(f\"\\nParsed {len(entries)} entries\")\n    \n    # ## Summary

I've generated ScummVM-ready code to parse and apply ALFRED.8 and ALFRED.B default state:

### Files Created:

1. **`alfred_room_defaults.h`** - C++ header for ScummVM integration
   - Contains static data tables for all 82 ALFRED.8 entries (33 rooms)
   - Contains static data tables for all 1180 ALFRED.B entries (28 rooms)  
   - Provides three functions:
     - `applyAlfred8Defaults(roomId, roomData, roomSize)` - Applies sprite positions, state flags, walkbox configs
     - `applyAlfredBDefaults(roomId, roomData, roomSize)` - Resets conversation "already seen" flags (writes 0x08)
     - `applyAllRoomDefaults(roomId, roomData, roomSize)` - Convenience function calling both

2. **`alfred_defaults.json`** - JSON data grouped by room (for reference/debugging)

3. **`generate_scummvm_defaults.py`** - The generator script

### ALFRED.8 Format (now fully decoded):

```
Entry: [room_id:2 LE][offset:2 LE][size:1][data:size bytes]
Terminator: 0xFFFF

Size byte IS the data length:
  0x01 = 1 byte (state flag)
  0x04 = 4 bytes (X,Y coordinate pair)
  0x12 = 18 bytes (walkbox/structured data)
```

### Key Room 14 Entry (walkbox example):
- **Offset 0x0213**: size=1, value=0x01 → **Walkbox count**
- **Offset 0x0221**: size=18, data=walkbox configuration → **Walkbox data block**

### ALFRED.B Format:
- All 1180 entries are identical format: `[room:2][offset:2][0x01][0x08]`
- All write value `0x08` to reset "conversation already seen" flags

### Usage in ScummVM:
```cpp
#include "alfred_room_defaults.h"

// When loading a room:
byte *roomData = loadRoomFromAlfred1(roomId);
uint32 roomSize = getRoomSize(roomId);

// Apply clean default state
Alfred::applyAllRoomDefaults(roomId, roomData, roomSize);

// Now apply your own saved state on top...
```

  "textEditContent": "# Copilot Instructions for alfredtools\n\n## Project Overview\nReverse engineering toolkit for **Alfred Pelrock** (1997 DOS point-and-click adventure game). Primary goal: complete ScummVM reimplementation.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Game Data Files (in &#96;files/&#96;)\n| File | Purpose | Size |\n|------|---------|------|\n| ALFRED.1 | Room data (backgrounds, sprites, text, hotspots, walkboxes, exits) | 12.9MB |\n| ALFRED.2 | Character talking animations (RLE compressed) | 2.1MB |\n| ALFRED.3 | Character movement animations | 311KB |\n| ALFRED.4 | UI graphics (popups, speech balloons) | 43KB |\n| ALFRED.5 | Shadow layers per room | 1.7MB |\n| ALFRED.6 | Overlay graphics (\"pegatinas\"/stickers) | 700KB |\n| ALFRED.7 | Sprites and cursors | 3.6MB |\n| ALFRED.8 | Room default state values (clean state) | 649B |\n| ALFRED.9 | Fonts, color remap tables | 146KB |\n| ALFRED.B | Conversation state reset flags | 7KB |\n\n### Key Data Structures\n- **ALFRED.1**: 56 rooms × 13 data pairs (offset+size). Room directory at 0x0000.\n- **Room offsets**: Pair 10 = hotspots/walkboxes/exits, Pair 11 = palette (768B), Pair 12 = text\n- **Walkbox**: 9 bytes each at room_data+0x218, count at +0x213\n- **Hotspot**: 9 bytes each at room_data+0x47C, count at +0x47A\n- **Exit**: 14 bytes each at room_data+0x1BF, count at +0x1BE\n\n## Build &amp; Run\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nmake          # Builds bin/alfredcli\nmake clean    # Removes bin/\nmake run      # Builds and runs\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### C Code (&#96;src/*.c&#96;)\n- Little-endian structs with &#96;#pragma pack(push, 1)&#96;\n- File paths hardcoded as &#96;files/ALFRED.*&#96;\n- Use &#96;lodepng&#96; for PNG output\n- Switch which extraction runs in &#96;main.c&#96; by commenting/uncommenting\n\n### Python Scripts (&#96;src/*.py&#96;, root &#96;*.py&#96;)\n- Standalone extraction/analysis scripts\n- Use &#96;struct.unpack('&lt;I', ...)&#96; for little-endian\n- Output to &#96;output_*/&#96; directories\n- Run directly: &#96;python3 src/extract_backgrounds.py&#96;\n\n### ImHex Patterns (&#96;*.hexpat&#96;)\n- Binary format definitions for game files\n- Use with ImHex to visualize structures\n\n## Key Documentation\n- [SAVE_GAME_SYSTEM_ANALYSIS.md](SAVE_GAME_SYSTEM_ANALYSIS.md) - Memory addresses, state structures\n- [RESOURCE_FILE_FORMAT_DOCUMENTATION.md](RESOURCE_FILE_FORMAT_DOCUMENTATION.md) - Complete ALFRED.* formats\n- [CONVERSATION_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md](CONVERSATION_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md) - Dialog/text control codes\n- [SHADOW_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md](SHADOW_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md) - Character shadows per room\n\n## Workflow Tips\n1. Check existing &#96;.md&#96; docs before analyzing - most systems are already documented\n2. Ghidra analysis available - see &#96;GHIDRA_*.md&#96; files for disassembly notes\n3. Use &#96;*.hexpat&#96; files with ImHex to explore binary structures\n4. Generated ScummVM code goes in &#96;src/scummvm/&#96; or &#96;alfred_*.h&#96; files\n5. All offsets are little-endian unless noted otherwise\n",
